name: moirai_run
description: Run the annotated application under moirai-service, a smoke run then the baseline, with live provenance on the Dashboard; also apps launched by a generated `flux batch` run.sh (Elmerfold): the app job runs a generated per-chunk submit wrapper (submit_moirai.sh, passed to run.sh as --submit-script) that starts moirai-service in its own shell; dry-run first. Load for the moirai_smoke and baseline stages, for 'flux batch', 'run.sh', 'submit-script', 'bulksubmit', 'drain', 'dftracer_service not found', 'spill-only', 'exclusive'.

history.why: Elmerfold is launched as `flux batch run.sh` (2 nodes + Rabbit, launch node drained). The old _script runs `flux run -N n moirai-service start`, which cannot place work on the drained launch node and never returns. Adds a batch mode (batch_script, queue) with a generated run-moirai.sh, a dry-run tool, and a per-host trace report.

User approved a 2-sequence smoke of Elmerfold on 2 nodes + Rabbit (40 min). Elmerfold launches as `flux batch run.sh` and drains the launch node, so the generic `flux run -N n moirai-service start` script cannot place services. Add a batch mode (run.sh rewritten with a moirai preamble and per-node pinned services), a dry-run tool, a dftracer_service resolver, and multi-host validation.

v3 starts the per-node moirai-service with a pinned detached `flux submit --requires=host:<h>`. A flux-submitted service is a scheduled job holding cores, so the app's own `flux bulksubmit --nodes 1 --exclusive` jobs may wait forever. Replaced by ONE mechanism, `flux exec -r all` (setsid nohup, detached), which bypasses the scheduler. Verified on Tuolumne 2026-10-30 (pdebug, 1-node alloc; /p/lustre5/haridev/elmerfold/runs/flux-exec-test.out and flux-exec-env.out): flux exec returns in 1 s, the process survives, `flux resource list` still shows 96 cores free and 0 allocated, `flux run -N1 --exclusive hostname` still runs, flux exec passes the caller's env and cwd, `-r all` reaches every rank, no `flux idset` exists. Same rank set for start, ring wait and stop, so no host drift.

Design change decided by the user. v3 rewrote the generated Elmerfold run.sh to start moirai-service as pinned detached `flux submit` jobs after the drain. Verified in the real run.sh (runs/moirai-smoke/run.sh, runs/smoke/run.sh): after the drain, prestage (`flux run --nodes $num_nodes --tasks-per-node 1`), the dbcast `flux run ... --exclusive` steps and the app job (`flux bulksubmit --nodes 1 --exclusive ... submit_smsp.sh '{}' ::: chunk.csv`) all need the whole worker node, so a one-core service job there blocks them until the limit. New design: a per-chunk submit wrapper (submit_moirai.sh) passed to the UNMODIFIED run.sh via --submit-script; it runs on the exclusive worker node, starts moirai-service in the background of its own shell, waits for the ring, runs the original submit_smsp.sh as a child, stops the service, keeps the rc. run.sh is no longer rewritten.

Fix A (pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944, moirai_smoke). gen_launch_script.py line 849-850 requires --submit-script to be an EXISTING file, but submit_moirai.sh was only written by moirai_smoke_run at submit time, so the documented order could not work. New tool moirai_wrapper_write writes only the wrapper (755, idempotent, sha256), moirai_smoke_run/baseline verify the on-disk wrapper against the fresh render and rewrite and report a mismatch; plan note/docs and Order of use updated. Added moirai_wrapper_selftest.

Pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944, moirai_smoke, first real submission (batch f3hFu78obrzb, wrapper job moirai-smoke-batch-934280540). D1 false pass: the per-chunk wrapper exited 2 ('moirai-wrapper: no dftracer_service found') but run.sh ended normally, so the batch was COMPLETED rc 0 and the wrapper job exited 0; run.out held 'flux-job: task(s) exited with exit code 2' and '<date>: f35QqToh9 failed'. The batch wrapper job now reads the batch --output file (parsed from run.sh '#flux: --output') and fails with distinct codes 20 (chunk failed, names job id and log), 21/22 (hosts.txt missing/empty), 23 (output file missing). D2 wrong resolver: moirai-service in the venv is a Python entry-point script, so dirname(readlink -f)/../../dftracer/bin is wrong; the wrapper now resolves the package through python (import dftracer), service_venv defaults from integrate outputs moirai.python and is verified at write time, and moirai_service_resolve reads the venv from the script shebang.

Two defects from the first real submission (pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944, batch job f3hFu78obrzb, wrapper job moirai-smoke-batch-934280540, 2026-10-30). D1 false pass: the per-chunk wrapper exited 2 (no dftracer_service found), the app never ran, but run.sh ends normally even when its flux bulksubmit chunk job fails, so the batch was COMPLETED rc 0 and the batch wrapper job exited 0; run.out held 'flux-job: task(s) exited with exit code 2' and '<date>: f35QqToh9 failed'. The batch wrapper job now reads the --output file named in run.sh's '#flux: --output' header and fails (exit 4, naming the chunk job id) on those lines, exit 5 when hosts.txt is missing or empty, exit 6 when the output file is unreadable. D2 wrong resolver: the fallback used dirname(readlink -f moirai-service)/../../dftracer/bin/dftracer_service, but the venv's moirai-service is a Python entry-point script. service_venv now defaults from integrate outputs moirai.python (venv root) and is verified at write time to hold an executable dftracer/bin/dftracer_service; the in-wrapper fallback resolves the package through python -c 'import dftracer'; moirai_service_resolve prefers the venv and reports binary_kind. Render is identical for an explicit or defaulted venv.
